profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting between the maintainer of a Nokia mobile-phone performance analysis tool and a device integration engineer after the tool started reporting impossible CPU utilization values and suspicious task timeline spikes on a new 5.14 firmware image used for an internal demo. The context is that a camera-launch slowdown was reproduced on a demo handset, and the latest traces show processor utilization above 100% plus unusually large UI-task execution blocks. The agenda is to decide whether the issue is caused by the handset software, the tracing configuration, or the analysis tool's report generation, and to agree on the next diagnostic run. The expected outcome is a short-term troubleshooting plan for a fresh trace capture and a working assumption about where the regression most likely sits before the demo.

members.name: Elina Vartiainen
members.expertise: Trace parsing, timing normalization, report generation for processor load and task execution analysis
members.background: Elina has maintained the PC-side performance analysis tool for three years and recently refactored the report pipeline that produces processor utilization and task execution statistics for Nokia handset teams.
members.private_state: She wants to determine whether the strange numbers come from trace interpretation rather than a real handset regression, because a parser bug introduced in the recent refactor would undermine confidence in the tool before the demo.
hidden_assumptions: "Baseline trace" refers to the standard 30-second post-boot capture taken after the handset has settled on the home screen.
Any handset labeled with the 5.14 demo image is also running tracing stub v3.2, which emits ISR entry and exit markers needed for IRQ exclusion.
If processor utilization totals exceed 100% by more than a couple of percent, the trace timestamps or parser normalization are suspect before the handset software is.
"Full instrumentation" means turning on all analyzer-supported task-switch and timing decoders already present in the trace, not rebuilding the firmware.

members.name: Jari Lehtonen
members.expertise: Handset firmware builds, trace hook enablement, lab reproductions on Nokia mobile-phone software
members.background: Jari owns the integration builds used in the device lab, coordinates trace captures on prototype phones, and works closely with subsystem teams when performance regressions appear in real handset workflows like camera launch and media playback.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the troubleshooting focused on the reproducible camera slowdown on the demo phone and avoid a time-consuming investigation into build variants unless absolutely necessary.
hidden_assumptions: "Baseline trace" means the standard symptom-reproduction window from the first camera keypress until preview appears.
If a handset carries the 5.14 image label, its tracing support is effectively equivalent for routine analysis, regardless of the exact tracing stub revision on that device.
A utilization report is "sane" if the top CPU-consuming tasks match the user-visible slowdown and the idle task drops as expected during the repro.
"Full instrumentation" means rebuilding the firmware with all kernel trace channels enabled and using aggressive buffer flushing so nothing is missed.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the baseline trace
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to comparing the new results against "the baseline trace."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the team's standard 30-second post-boot idle-to-home-screen capture used to validate report stability and load accounting.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the standard camera-launch reproduction trace from keypress to preview, usually 6-8 seconds long, used in device performance triage.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams genuinely use the phrase "baseline trace" in routine work, and each version is considered the obvious default for performance troubleshooting, so neither thinks to spell out the capture window.

misalignment_points.topic: Whether IRQ time is already excluded
misalignment_points.surface_form: They speak as if task execution statistics "already exclude IRQ time."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the demo handset is running tracing stub v3.2, which emits interrupt markers that let the tool subtract ISR time from task execution statistics.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the 5.14 firmware label is sufficient and does not realize one demo phone still has an older tracing stub that lacks the needed ISR markers.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The tracing-stub revision is treated as low-level setup that was supposedly standardized earlier, so both participants talk past the device-specific variation without suspecting a hidden dependency.

misalignment_points.topic: What makes the utilization report look sane
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both evaluate whether the utilization report "looks sane."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the average processor load and per-task totals should reconcile mathematically to roughly 100% over the analyzed interval, within a small tolerance.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the ranking and shape of the busiest tasks should match the observed slowdown pattern, even if the totals are imperfect.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In troubleshooting conversations, "sane" is a casual shorthand rather than a formal acceptance criterion, so each applies the standard that matters in their own role without realizing the other is using a different test.

misalignment_points.topic: What to do for a full instrumentation rerun
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to rerun the case with "full instrumentation."
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a rerun using the existing firmware but with all available analyzer-side decoders and task-switch timing reports enabled, mainly to test parsing and timestamp normalization.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects to rebuild the handset image with extra kernel channels, additional trace hooks, and more aggressive buffer flushing before recapturing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each person controls a different part of the toolchain and naturally interprets "full instrumentation" as the fullest version of the settings they personally manage, so the phrase falsely signals agreement.

Before anyone blames the handset image, I want to anchor this against the standard 30-second post-boot settled capture we use to sanity-check load accounting. If the same parser path misbehaves there, this could be my recent refactor in trace interpretation or normalization, not a real regression on the phone.

turns.inner_thought: From my side, that still sounds usable enough.
